interpretation:
Scripted units, not a model: the drifter is the learner-style unit that changes slugify's signature in place, edits the vendored helper, writes configuration at the repository root, writes a rule into the README and edits the identity's glossary — and repeats every one of them after a repair hint. Under the control arm the first six tasks close and every drift lands on main: the two-parameter slugify, the vendor edit, config.json and .env, the README rule, the glossary edit. Under the treatment arm none of the seven closes: the first unit is refused three times by the export-signature check and stops at the attempt ceiling, and every later unit finds the known defect still on main, re-applies the same two-parameter fix, and is refused the same way, with identity-untouched adding the vendor and identity edits to the record and glossary-lint the comment that calls a unit a task. This is the row where the gated arm loses, and it loses completely on throughput: zero closed against six, three attempts per unit against one on the first six, and a replan owed to S3 per unit — the recovery policy's third check-failure is replan, not escalate, so nothing reached a person, which is its own finding about the policy. It wins on what the suite pre-registered: signature drift on main is zero against one, and every violation is a recorded refusal rather than a merge. The ablation arms are less informative against this unit than lesson 14's were, and the report should say why rather than pretend: the drifter trips three checks on its very first unit — the signature probe, and glossary-lint on the comment that calls slugify a task — so removing any one of them leaves another to refuse the same unit, and every ablation arm closes nothing, like the treatment. Only the control arm, with none of them, lands the drift. A per-regulator contribution needs a unit that trips one check at a time; the sloppy report's no-glossary-lint arm is that case. Two things the report does not show. The root-level config.json and .env pass every closeout check in every arm — only the boundary grader sees them, because in a live session the profile grant (and, since lesson 15, the instance manifest's declared prefixes) would refuse the write, and a scripted unit never runs a session. And a stubborn unit that will not repair is a unit the recovery policy should hand to a person sooner than the third attempt: the cost here is the policy's, not the gates'.

The seventh task, d7-archive (#201 item 11), needs the fact d5 should have recorded: the archive tests pass only once test/archive.test.js sets its clock to UTC. The drifter remembered nothing at d5 (it wrote the TZ rule into the README), and at d7 it writes the rule into the README again and sets no clock, so the archive tests fail under every arm, control included: three attempts and three refusals each, the README rule repeated on every repair, and the control arm's only unclosed task. Under the treatment and the ablation arms d7 is refused on its other drifts as well (the signature, and the inherited suite where that check runs), like every drifter unit there. So this row is where both arms lose equally on attempts, and it says nothing about memory helping, since no arm had a fact to render: a rule in prose is not memory, and nothing reads it. A scripted unit reads no context, so "used the remembered fact" is enacted from the records (the arm renders memory and the store holds a current fact about TZ), not observed: these rows show the plumbing and the grader, and whether a model sets the clock from memory, or finds it again from d5's comment in test/dated.test.js or from the failure, is the second live report's reading (#201). And d7's row is a position in a sequence, not a trial of its own: it includes everything d1 to d6 left on main. This report ran suite version 4 (version 2 added d7, version 3 `cost` and `cacheShare`, version 4 the planner-quality counts); it is comparable with the other version-4 reports and not with the first live report, which ran version 1.

The planner-quality counts (#49) move on one thing here: the replan S3 decides on a unit's third refusal, counted as a miss on the attempt the second repair hint was handed to (`replansDecided` and `missesAtAttempt` 1, `missesPerHandoff` one in three). That is every unit of the treatment and the four ablation arms, and d7 alone under control, so the gated arm "loses" on the handoff counts by a separated margin — because it refuses, not because its contracts are worse: the contracts and the reports are the same in every arm. The counts read what the records say, and the drifter's reports say nothing: it changes the fixed signature on every unit and never reports a deviation, so `fixedDeviations` is zero in every run, control included, while `signatureDrift` and the export-signature check see the change. A fixed decision broken silently is the outcome graders' to measure, not this one's.
